newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Centrum completing another acquisition.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Centrum completing another acquisition.

text.p: Centrum Industries Inc expects to take its building-through-acquisitions strategy one step further this week when it completes the purchase of Taylor Forge International Inc.

"I have no reason to believe that we won't be making a pretty decent profit out of Taylor in the July-to-September quarter," said Centrum president George Wells, who disclosed the acquisition in a telephone interview Tuesday.
Privately-held Taylor Forge, a Memphis, Tenn.-based manufacturer of steel seamless rings with sales of about $10 million, has been running close to breakeven for the past couple of years.
It's just the kind of company Centrum is seeking in its strategy of rejuventating underperforming operations and melding them into a manufacturing conglomerate.
"This is a pretty significant strategic acquisition for us," Wells said.
It apparently won't be the last. Wells said Centrum is in discussions with two companies in materials handling and machine tools and expects one of the two deals to close this fiscal year.
"I expect certainly one more transaction in fiscal 1998," Wells said.

Wells said Centrum will combine Taylor Forge with its McInnes Steel subsidiary to create one of the largest suppliers in North America of seamless rings which are used by the oil industry and in aerospace, off-road construction and mining equipment.
Taylor Forge's operations, which include one plant and about 75 employees, were purchased in a cash and stock transaction valued at about $7 million.
Centrum hopes to increase sales of Taylor Forge to $12 million to $13 million within the next 12 to 18 months.
Centrum's operations consist of three manufacturing businesses.
Micafil was acquired in May 1993 and makes production machinery for motors used in the automotive and consumer durable goods markets.
American Handling, acquired in September 1993, provides material handling systems for warehouses and distribution centers.
In March 1996, Centrum acquired McInnes Steel which makes specialty steel forgings for the power generation and compressor industries.

Centrum expects to report results for its fiscal year ended March 31 during the June 23 week. The company estimates its fiscal 1997 earnings will increase to about $2.3 million or $0.28 a share from $805,000 and $0.13 a year earlier. Sales are estimated at more than $70 million, up from the $27.5 million in the fiscal 1996 year.
Looking ahead to fiscal 1998, Centrum expects results to benefit from acquisitions and estimates sales will be in the low to mid-$80 million range.
Shares of Holland, Ohio-based Centrum last traded at 2-3/32.
